newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan chip makers to cut investment in 97/98 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan chip makers to cut investment in 97/98 - paper.

text.p: Total capital investment by Japan's top five semiconductor makers in the year from April 1 will be 750 billion yen, down nearly 10 percent from the estimated actual investment in the current year, a Japanese business daily said on Tuesdasy.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said NEC Corp, the largest of the five makers, planned to maintain the same level of capital investment in 1997/98 as in 1996/97, but the other four -- Toshiba Corp, Hitachi Ltd, Fujitsu Ltd and Mitsubishi Electric Corp -- planned investment about 10 percent lower.
The makers were not immediately available for comment.

The paper said the smaller investment was because the makers thought a fall in prices of the popular 16-megabit dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chips would continue and this would squeeze their profits.
